title: Persistence: snapshotting, the append-only file and the durability of each

videos.script: Every key in Redis lives in memory. {{memory}} So the question for any Redis that holds real data is simple. What is left after the process dies? Redis has two answers, and this lesson kills a server to measure each. {{two}} The first is a snapshot. Every few minutes the whole dataset goes into one file. A crash loses everything written since. {{snapshot}} The second is a log. Every write is appended to a file, and a restart replays it. {{log}} How much the log can lose depends on one setting: how often Redis asks the disk to really keep what it wrote. {{fsync}} Asking after every write is the safest choice, and you will measure what it costs. {{benchmark}} Then the trap. Turn the log on the obvious way, and Redis starts empty, with your data in a file it never reads. {{trap}} You will see it happen, and then do it the safe way. {{safe}}
